clue.text: Violent storm encountered on the way back — bother!
Shipment miles away from Channel?

indicators.note: something away from a place is no longer in it, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for miles
to channel something is to pass it on

explanation.surface: Goods being sent a long way off from the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' with its capital letter looks like the sea between England and France, but it is a verb meaning pass on.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the conveying of goods from one place to another, so it can stand for shipment.

clue.text: Cat that hunts across river for chevrotain

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so one piece stretches around the other

blocks.note: a mouser is a cat valued for catching mice
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A hunting cat goes over the river after a small deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The chevrotain is a tiny hoofed animal of Asian and African forests, commonly called the mouse deer.

clue.text: One may be employed by one before retiring

definitions.text: One may be employed by one before retiring

blocks.clueFragment: One may be employed by one before retiring
blocks.note: surface reading: someone is hired by a person about to stop working
setter's reading: retiring means going to bed, and the thing is used to warm the bed beforehand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Employed' and 'retiring' suggest a job and a pension; retiring here means going to bed, and employed means used.
explanation.definitionFit: This heated bed covering is switched on to warm the bed before someone goes to sleep.

clue.text: Bucket down in stable, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or told, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a stable is a group of racehorses, wrestlers or drivers working together, a team

explanation.surface: Rain pours down on a horse's stable.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucket down is British for rain heavily; 'stable' looks like a building but is a group of performers under one owner.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem with rain and to bucket down both mean to rain very heavily, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Protestant bishop suitable? It's doubtful

indicators.note: when something is doubtful it is uncertain and unsettled, so these letters are not in their final order

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
apt means suitable
the three letters of the word rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a bishop is right for a Protestant post and decides it is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'It's doubtful' look like a comment on the bishop; it is the shuffled 'It's' that ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baptist belongs to a Protestant denomination practising adult baptism by immersion, so it is one example of a Protestant.

clue.text: Detain someone in conversation, but not round hovel

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before being turned
a hole is a dingy, wretched dwelling

explanation.surface: Someone is kept talking, though not about a shabby little house.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole someone is an idiom for stopping them and keeping them in a conversation they may not want.

clue.text: I favour top range rattles for the little angel

indicators.note: rattles means shakes about, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: all fifteen letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper prefers the best toy rattles to buy for a sweet baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rattles' looks like a noun, babies' toys, but it is a verb meaning shakes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A little angel is an ironic or fond name for a perfectly behaved person, which is a model of goodness.

clue.text: Home, small apartment, not suitable

blocks.note: at home means in
APT is the short form of apartment

explanation.surface: A tiny flat makes an unsuitable home.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means inappropriate or unfitting, so it is a synonym for not suitable.

clue.text: Film in that place must involve outside broadcast

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so the first piece holds the second

blocks.note: in that place means there
OB is the broadcasting abbreviation for an outside broadcast

explanation.surface: Shooting a movie on location needs an outside broadcast unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Robe is a 1953 Biblical epic, the first film released in CinemaScope, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Where many a bandit may be sent into a spin

definitions.text: Where many a bandit may be sent into a spin

blocks.clueFragment: Where many a bandit may be sent into a spin
blocks.note: surface reading: a hideout where outlaws are thrown into confusion
setter's reading: a one-armed bandit is a slot machine whose reels spin, found in rows at a seaside gaming hall

explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a coin-operated fruit machine; its reels are set spinning, and such machines fill seaside gaming halls.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a venue full of coin-operated games, including many fruit machines whose reels spin.

clue.text: Afternoon nap in cosiest armchair

indicators.note: in says the word sits inside the run of letters that follows, spanning two words

blocks.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone takes an afternoon doze in the most comfortable armchair in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is the Spanish custom of a short rest or sleep after lunch, so an afternoon nap.

clue.text: Rowed all the way, never gave up

blocks.note: rowed in the sense of quarrelled, rhyming with 'cowed'
going all the way means going right to the end

explanation.surface: An oarsman kept pulling right to the line without giving in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowed' reads as rowing a boat, but here it is the other pronunciation, meaning had a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight something to the finish is an idiom for persisting until the end, which is never giving up.

clue.text: Biscuit may give stimulation, taken with instant

blocks.note: ginger means liveliness or spirit, as in to ginger up
a snap decision is an instant one

explanation.surface: A biscuit gives a quick boost when eaten straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger snap is a crisp, thin biscuit flavoured with ginger, so it is a kind of biscuit.

clue.text: See 11
Regular returned carrying right bottle

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: regular, as in uniform or steady, is even
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pub regular came back with the right bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, as in 'lose your bottle'; the pub scene makes it look like a container of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve and bottle are both informal words for courage or daring, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Phone — who invented it? Sound familiar?
Odd-looking brush plant

indicators.note: something odd-looking appears strange or out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange-looking bristly plant in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree, so it is one kind of plant.

clue.text: Skiffs, in the morning, passing through bridges

indicators.note: passing through means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a span is a bridge or the stretch it covers
AM is the abbreviation for the morning hours, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: Small boats float under the bridges early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampans are small flat-bottomed boats of East Asia, comparable to skiffs, which are light small boats.

clue.text: On west of island, daughter is pecked by game bird

indicators.note: being pecked puts one thing inside the beak of another, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: golf is a game
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm

explanation.surface: On the western side of an island a girl is pecked by a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' looks like one phrase, but game is the sport and bird alone is the definition. 'On west of island' places the first part before the island word.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldfinch is a small songbird with a red face and yellow wing bars, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Barbaric male leader of Amazons, at that time

indicators.note: the leader is whoever comes first, so only the initial letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
the first letter of the word
at that time means then

explanation.surface: A savage man leads a tribe of warrior women in some past era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barbaric' is used as an adjective; heathen can be one too, meaning uncivilised.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathen as an adjective means uncivilised or pagan, close in sense to barbaric.

clue.text: Wholesale slaughter in ancient city following religious ceremony

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so the city's name is placed second

blocks.note: the Mass is the Catholic service of the Eucharist
Acre is an ancient port city in present-day Israel

explanation.surface: A massacre takes place in an old city right after a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the city after the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the killing of many people at once, which is what wholesale slaughter means.

clue.text: Opening of sewage farm, in spite of this

indicators.note: the opening is where a word begins, so its first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to farm land is to till it

explanation.surface: A sewage works opens despite objections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Farm' looks like a noun after 'sewage', but it is the verb meaning cultivate.
explanation.definitionFit: Still as an adverb means nevertheless, which is the same as in spite of this.

clue.text: Managed to bump into Spanish aunt in capital

indicators.note: bumping into something means going into it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: tía is the Spanish word for aunt
managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone happened to meet their Spanish aunt while in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Terrified, initially, to embrace ruffian

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to embrace is to hug

explanation.surface: A frightened person is grabbed by a violent thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug is a violent, rough criminal, so it is a synonym for ruffian.

clue.text: Such a hurtful rebuff may knock the smile off one's face!

definitions.text: Such a hurtful rebuff may knock the smile off one's face!

blocks.note: surface reading: a cruel rejection that leaves someone unhappy

blocks.clueFragment: knock the smile off one's face
blocks.note: setter's reading: literally, a blow to the mouth that knocks out the teeth one smiles with

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a cruel setback is read literally: a blow to the mouth would remove the teeth that make a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a harsh disappointment or humiliating rejection, especially from someone unexpected.

clue.text: Part of Croatian resort, elevated

blocks.note: Split is a resort city on Croatia's Adriatic coast
elevated means raised, up

explanation.surface: A section of a Croatian holiday town that stands on high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a noun, a piece of the resort, but it is the verb meaning separate.
explanation.definitionFit: To part, as a couple does, is to separate, and split up is the everyday phrasal verb for that.

clue.text: Sprite in ring formed round diseased elm

indicators.note: formed means shaped into something new, so the letters before it are rearranged
round means going around the outside, so one piece wraps the other
diseased suggests something unhealthy and out of order, so those letters are rearranged too

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A woodland spirit dances in a fairy ring around a sick elm tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary mischievous creature blamed for mechanical faults, a kind of sprite or imp.
